title: Milenburg camps and Smokey Mary
summary: Asked about Milenburg, he recalls the camps near the lake and the Smokey Mary train.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I think that's a good idea. Jimmy Clayton was telling us some of the hazards of traveling a few weeks ago. Did you ever play at Milenburg or any of those places in town?
Milenburg, yeah, I played back Milenburg. Before the...
When did they tear down, I mean, when did they fill in and tear down all those camps out there? Well, to tell you...
How long did that last? That must have come way back round by round 1925, to tell you the truth. Way back in there.
When you started playing in 29 or so, did they still have some camps out there?

Well, they had a few spots where all the roads hadn't built up. You take a Lesion Field hadn't built up. They just only paved a Lesion Field all the way back, said during the... Just a little before the wall. Yep. Just a little before the wall. We had a lot of roads that wasn't built in. But I remember when Lesion Field was the only street that was going back to the lake, you'd have the train used to go back in the center of Lesion Field, Smokey Mary. I heard about that. Yeah, Smokey Mary used to go in there.
